business_problem: Wimbledon needed a way to produce informative, engaging narrated tennis clips at scale while preserving the sport-specific language and tone fans expect.
solution_summary: The All England Club used foundation models from watsonx as the AI layer behind Wimbledon match-clip narration, training the models on the unique language of tennis so generated commentary would sound informative and sport-specific rather than generic. In this implementation, generative AI is applied directly to media production: tennis content is turned into clips, the model produces narration with varied sentence structure and vocabulary, and the output is designed to make those clips more engaging for fans. Although the page is brief, it clearly positions watsonx as more than a general experimentation platform; IBM's foundation models are being adapted to a domain-specific vocabulary and then used to automate part of the editorial experience around a flagship sports event. The result is a content-generation workflow that blends AI language models with Wimbledon media assets to create richer digital storytelling at scale.
